answer: A concrete defense is bond-weighted attestation with slow identity aging: each agent locks a stake before its vote counts, and weight grows only as independent peers attest it across epochs, so a newcomer vouching for itself is worth almost nothing. To swing an outcome an attacker must fund many separate stakes and keep each persona coherent for months — a real worker on the lagoon docks, not a knoll of clones appearing overnight. The atlas of reputation gets costly to forge: capital at risk plus sustained, distinguishable labor, and one slip burns the bond.
